Music
Music is such an important part of everyone’s daily lives. Here at Wyvern we believe that it’s a powerful and unique form of communication enriching and enhancing the lives of everyone that it touches. It can change the way in which we feel, think and act. How often does music trigger a memory or emotion?
Music at Wyvern give everyone a level playing field on which to work together. Pupils learn to turn-take, communicate, gain confidence, and explore and listen to various instruments and musical genres.
Music at Wyvern has come on in leaps and bounds this year, with sessions running weekly and proving popular among students across the school. Some students have formed super groups and worked on ensemble pieces to perform at the end of term, and others have performed solo pieces with great success. Talented local musician, Gary Pickard, has helped run these sessions, and engaged with the pupils fantastically to bring out the best of their musical skills with an emphasis on enjoyment.
Lucy Ardagh, Music Lead

Wyvern Academy Website
Art at Wyvern
At Wyvern we aim to encourage students to investigate, interpret and respond to the world around them through a broad range of media and techniques. Students are introduced to art and artists from a variety of different cultures and time periods and given space and opportunities to explore materials and processes with appropriate support.
Art and design is a vital part of a child’s development, and the ability to mimic, interpret and express feelings is crucial in all our lives. Creating art and working with different materials also carries a high sensory load which allows SEND pupils to access the curriculum in a broader sense than other subjects.
Art and design are taught in weekly lessons in each class, and are also embedded into daily routines as a sensory and expressive method of understanding for many pupils. Working with their hands, and creating a physical, tangible object which can be touched and felt can help many of our students to process information and respond to stimulus.
We strongly value the importance of the arts as it is fantastic way for our pupils to express themselves in a variety of forms. We are aware of the value of the arts as a whole package and we promote the importance of music, art, dance and drama in every classroom and across each department.
We deliver high quality arts across the school hence ensuring every child and young person has the opportunity to experience the richness of the arts through creative planning and a breadth of engaging resources.

Wyvern Academy Website
The Local Governing Board
(For Southern Education Trust Board and Members information click here.)
Meet the Governors
I am a retired commercial solicitor, having spent most of my career in the financial services industry. I was a governor of my sons’ secondary school for 13 years, including 3 years as chair of governors.
My wife and I live in Weymouth, my wife’s family coming from Portland.
I enjoy watching football and tennis, walking, reading, theatre and cinema.
I joined the Board at the end of 2023; this is my first role in a governing body, and I look forward to helping support the school in providing an effective education for all. I moved to Dorset in 1993 to take up an Engineering position with the Ministry of Defence. I then moved into the education sector as a Maths teacher and have worked in a large comprehensive school in Dorchester for 25 years, where I have been fortunate to hold a variety of teaching positions and am currently an Assistant Headteacher.
When I am not working, I am an avid reader and enjoy a round of golf, which I have taken up relatively recently. I also enjoy travel, and try to get back to Scotland to visit family when I can.
I joined the Board in September 2025 as a parent governor. My son has attended Wyvern since 2018. I’m currently a director of two companies co-owned with my husband and have previously worked in banking, the civil service and also at Weymouth College in various administrative roles.
I enjoy walking in nature, swimming, meditation and collecting crystals (I love a bit of woo-woo!).
I look forward to helping support the Academy in its strategic direction moving forward.
I joined Wyvern Academy’s board of Governors in 2019, initially as a parent trustee, when my son attended Wyvern, and soon after took on the role as Safeguarding Governor.
I’m also a trustee with Action CP, a national charity that advocates for policy change and greater public, professional and political awareness of issues relating to children with cerebral palsy and their families. My campaign work for them has included lobbying MPs in Westminster and addressing members of both houses of Parliament for the All Party Parliamentary Group (APPG) for cerebral palsy.
As a parent of a child with special needs, I understand what hopes parents have for their children’s education when they start school, and I am glad to be playing a part in ensuring that Wyvern Academy is continually striving to offer the very best to its pupils.
Having grown up in north Dorset, after I qualified as a doctor from St George’s, I returned to the county and settled in Weymouth. I feel very lucky to live on the Jurassic coast, the perfect place to bring up my son.
In my spare time I enjoy a number of hobbies – writing children’s stories, folk and acoustic music, and yoga.
Dave Allen: Community Governor
I became a member of the Board of Governors in September 2025. After working in mainstream Secondary schools as an English teacher and eventually SENCO at Purbeck School, l joined the teaching staff at Wyvern in 1998 . I retired as a full time teacher in 2010.
Since then l have worked part time as a Horticultural therapist for adults with Special Needs and recovering addicts, an SEN tutor at West Highland College (Scotland) and tutor at Kingston Maurward College. I currently work as a volunteer with Dorset Council teaching English to refugee families in their homes.
Without doubt, Wyvern was my most rewarding, interesting, challenging ,exhausting job l had in education. It was also my most enjoyable.
As Governor l wish to support Wyvern as it continues to develop and thrive.
I love all sport especially tennis, football, cycling and even shinty! I also like fishing, reading and travelling.

Wyvern Academy Website
MOVE
The MOVE Programme is an activity-based framework for special schools like Wyvern. It has been specifically designed to help children with physical difficulties gain independent mobility—specifically sitting, standing, walking, and transitioning—to improve their learning, health, and independence. It combines education, therapy, and family input, allowing us to integrate functional movement into daily routines rather than just therapy sessions.
MOVE Centre of Excellence Award
Wyvern Academy is a holder of the prestigious MOVE Centre of Excellence Award.
Leading the way
Wyvern Academy is leading the way in providing children and young people with opportunities to develop independence and mobility. MOVE has been adopted by the Academy to develop the functional skills of children and young people with profound and complex physical disabilities.
What is MOVE?
MOVE Partnership has recently merged with the Enham trust, together they share the same vision and philosophy, that movement is the foundation for learning. The MOVE programme uses the combined knowledge of the family, carers, education and therapy. It is designed to teach anyone who has not learnt to sit, stand, walk or transfer by the age they would expect to, or those who have lost these skills, to increase their independent mobility to the best of their ability.
Embracing the principles of MOVE
Wyvern Academy has embraced MOVE and introduced the principles of the programme throughout the school. We currently have a number of children and young people on the programme with clear individualised goals; the goals are integrated into the curriculum with regular opportunities to practise skills and increase mobility.
Social inclusion
The programme has the potential to impact on every aspect of life not only for the individual, their family and care teams but for society as a whole. As our children and young people develop their mobility skills they can begin to take a more active role in their life.
Enhancing education
MOVE has been successfully implemented within the school, complementing and improving our approach to education and learning. The MOVE programme enhances the curriculum and enables children and young people to access learning more effectively. Children and young people appear more confident, motivated and engaged.
Impact
The MOVE programme has been hugely successful, with a number of children and young people progressing through the programme and into graduation. Children and young people on the programme are acquiring and maintaining skills that are then generalised into every aspect of their daily lives, allowing them to access their community and to become part of society.
Teachers have noticed a difference in cognition; children and young people are more engaged and receptive to teaching and learning.
MOVE has had a significant impact on families, improved mobility has increased access to the local community, allowing families to socialise and enjoy leisure activities together. Family life has improved within the home, increased function and mobility has developed independence, requiring less support from parents and carers.

Wyvern Academy Website
Latest Report
Our last Ofsted inspection took place in November 2024. The school was judged to have taken effective action to maintain the standards identified at the previous inspection which were Good in all aspects. The full report is available below but the summary reads as follows:
Wyvern Academy has a ‘child-centred, family-focused’ approach at the heart of its work.The school provides high-quality pastoral support to pupils and their families. It teachespupils how to stay safe, healthy and keep active. Pupils talk openly about differences andhow they are ‘the same but different’. Pupils flourish because of the nurturingrelationships and expert support they receive from staff.
The school has high expectations of pupils. It places high importance on a bespokecurriculum, including individualised therapeutic approaches to meet pupils’ needs. Pupilsbenefit from a strong focus on communication, early reading, writing and mathematics.They experience success because staff understand their individual needs extremely well.
Pupils’ behaviour in school is impressive. They behave well in lessons and socialsituations. When pupils struggle with their emotions, staff take effective and supportiveaction, which enables them to re-engage with their learning.
The provision for pupils’ wider development is well considered. Pupils enjoy theopportunities on offer, such as music, including the open orchestra, and sports. Theseactivities develop pupils’ interests and talents well.
Click here to read a copy of the full report or click here to see it via Ofsted’s website.

Wyvern Academy Website
Parent Voice
It is our strong belief that working closely with parents/carers is vital to the successful education and development of all pupils. To this end we engage with parents/carers in the widest possible variety of forums including parents’ evenings, coffee mornings, workshops, home/school diaries to name but a few.
A particular focus, on an annual basis, is placed on formal consultation in the form of a survey/questionnaire. This survey asks parents/carers to consider a variety of issues, for example the provision of after school activities, school lunches, or the effectiveness of communication between school and home. Along with all of the other channels of information sharing, these surveys help to guide certain directions that we might or might not be taking at Wyvern.
The feedback from this year’s survey was overwhelmingly positive once again. Families have told us how happy and supported their children feel here. In the comments, “amazing,” “supportive,” “lovely,” and “perfect” came up repeatedly. Parents have praised the individual effort we put in, the strong relationships we build, and how happy their children are at school, with many describing Wyvern as “the best place” for their child.
Some of the most appreciated aspects included:
Parents have told us that their children love coming to school, are thriving emotionally and academically, and feel valued and happy.
Parents are also very welcome and indeed encouraged to give their views at any time to the Ofsted site Parent View which allows comments on 12 different aspects of Wyvern, from the quality of teaching to dealing with bullying and behaviour. Parent View can be found at http://parentview.ofsted.gov.uk/.
